label: 01 / THE PROBLEM
title: A chargeback. A pile of records.
lines: Proposed response and evidence for review
note: Goal: less manual case assembly, with merchant control.
speech: For small online merchants, a chargeback starts a race to assemble records. The order, delivery history, customer messages, and response policy sit in different places. Rebuttal brings those records together, recommends a response, and drafts evidence for review. The goal is less manual case assembly, with the merchant retaining control of consequential decisions.

label: 02 / HOW IT WORKS
title: Evidence first. Then a decision.
tag: AWS STRANDS AGENTS SDK / APPLICATION DESIGN
lines: Strategy waits for all four collectors
Executor pauses when approval is required
note: Seven evidence graph nodes, plus a separate executor.
speech: Rebuttal uses the AWS Strands Agents SDK. After intake, four agents collect evidence in parallel. Strategy waits for all four. The drafter then receives both the evidence and the proposed response. A separate executor uses an approval hook before taking a guarded action.

label: 03 / RECORDING SETUP
title: A local run. A test environment.
note: Reveals follow the narration; waiting time is compressed.
speech: The next scenes replay a recorded local run. The merchant records are synthetic, and the Stripe objects are in test mode. The screen is an edited presentation of captured output, so reveals follow the narration rather than the original wait times. The owner response comes through the developer command line.

label: 06 / THE OWNER DECISION
title: The executor waits for a decision.
lines: Selected response resumes the Strands interrupt
The recorder then checks Stripe again
note: Developer command line; phone notification delivery is disabled.
speech: The approval step is a deliberate decision point. In this recording, the developer command line stands in for the merchant interface. Fight, concede, and hold are the three available responses. The selected response is passed back to the Strands interrupt, after which the recorder checks Stripe again. Phone notification delivery is disabled for this local demonstration.

After resuming, the recorder reads Stripe again. Compare the before and after states. That readback establishes the test result, not a real-world dispute outcome.

label: 09 / WHAT THIS DEMONSTRATES
title: A clearer dispute response workflow.
lines: A proposed strategy and draft response
An explicit owner decision before guarded actions
Synthetic merchant data and Stripe TEST objects
note: Real merchant outcomes and live phone delivery remain unverified.
speech: Rebuttal gives small merchants a place to review the facts, the proposed response, and the next action. This prototype runs locally with synthetic merchant data and Stripe test objects. Real merchant outcomes and live phone delivery remain outside this demonstration. The goal is a clearer, more controlled dispute workflow.
